questions.question: Which of the following food additives are helpful to combine products containing immiscible food ingredients, such as oil and water, with one another?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Food** **emulsifiers.**

 
• **Food emulsifiers** are additives that help combine immiscible ingredients, such as oil and water, in food products.
 
• They stabilize the mixture by reducing surface tension between the two substances, preventing separation.
 
• **Food** **Preservatives**:
 
 
• Purpose: Extend the shelf life of food products by inhibiting the growth of microorganisms.
 
• Examples: Sodium benzoate, potassium sorbate.
 
 
 
• **Food** **Stabilizers**:
 
 
• Purpose: Improve the texture and consistency of food products by preventing separation or crystallization.<

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of under eating?

options.text: Eating unusually large amounts of food with no apparent change in weight

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eating unusually large amounts of food with no apparent change in weight.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• During a time when **food **was in **short supply**, our **bodies evolved**.
 
• We are therefore **wired **to **maintain **our **weight**.
 
• When we start **losing body fat**, the **brain senses **problems because it** cannot tell **the **difference **between **healthy weight loss **and **famine**.
 
• As a result, it sets off a range of **intricate hormonal mechanisms **intended to stop us from **losing too much weight.**
 
• To put it another way, most attempts to **lose weight **ultimately fail not because a **person lacks willpower **but rather because we are **physically fighting **against the **inbuilt**, **primal biology **that is designed to keep us alive.
 
• This potent **anti-starvation mechanism **is activated by **eating too little**, which can undermine your efforts to slim down or even maintain a healthy weight in a number of ways. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Bulimia **is a disorder that involves eating an **unusual amount of food at once** (called **bingeing**), and then getting rid of it.
 
• To do this, one may **vomit **or use **laxatives **to **eliminate **the **food **from the body (called **purging**).
 
• Some **bulimics fast **(don't eat) or **over-exercise** after binges to **prevent weight **gain.
 
• **Water pills, laxatives, or diet pills** may also be used by **bulimics **to "**manage**" their weight.
 
• **Bulimics **frequently attempt to **cover up **their **bingeing **and **purging**.
 
• They might **stow **away food for **binges**.
 
• Bulimics are often within a few pounds of **normal weight**, however, their **weight **may **fluctuate**.

questions.question: Probiotics can be defined as:

options.text: endotoxin producing bacteria, which can lead to diarrhoea
live microorganisms that are intended to have health benefits when consumed or applied to the body
live microorganisms that pose a health threat when consumed or applied to the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__****Probiotics:**

__
 
• **Probiotics **are **live microorganisms **that are intended to **enhance health**.
 
• They can be found in **yoghurt **and other **fermented foods**, **dietary supplements**, and **cosmetics**. ***Hence Option 3 is correct.***
 
• Although bacteria and other microorganisms are sometimes thought of as **harmful **"**germs**," many of them are in fact **helpful**.
 
• Some bacteria help with **food digestion**, the production of **vitamins**, and the **destruction of disease-causing cells.**
 
• Numerous **probiotic bacteria **are identical to or nearly related to those that **naturally occur in our bodies.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• In probiotics, **various bacteria **could be present.
 
• The most common types of bacteria are those from the families **Lactobacillus **and **Bifidobacterium**.
 
• Other bacteria as well as yeasts like **Saccharomyces boulardii **may be used as probiotics.
 
• There are many different types of probiotics, and each has **potential effects**.
 
• For instance, just because one **strain **of **Lactobacillus **helps prevent a disease** doesn't mean that all strains of the bacteria** or all probiotics from the **Bifidobacterium **genus will do the same.

questions.question: Which of the following adulterants is mixed with sunflower oil and sesame oil to increase their quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Argemone oil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Argemone oil** is extracted from the **seeds of the Argemone plant**, also known as **prickly poppy or Mexican poppy**.
 
• It is mixed with **sunflower oil and sesame oil** to increase their quantity.
 
• The oil is commonly used in** traditional medicine** for its** anti-inflammatory **and **analgesic** properties.
 
• Argemone oil is also used in the **manufacturing of soaps, paints, and varnishes**.
 
• The oil contains toxic compounds called **alkaloids**, which can be harmful if ingested in large quantities.
 
• In some cultures, Argemone oil is used as a** cooking oil**, but its consumption has been linked to** health issues** such as epidemic dropsy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mustard Oil:**​

 
 
• Mustard oil is derived from the seeds of the** mustard plant** and is commonly used in **Indian and Bangladeshi cuisine**.
 
• It has a** high smoking point**, making it suitable for** frying and cooking** at high temperatures.
 
• Mustard oil is rich in **monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats**, which are beneficial for heart health.
 
• The oil is also used in traditional medicine for its **antibacterial and anti-fungal properties**.
 
• Mustard oil has a** pungent flavor** and is often used as a** flavoring agent** in dishes.
 
 

 
• **Lentil Oil:**

 
 
• ​Lentil oil is extracted from the** seeds of lentils**, which are **legumes** commonly used in cooking.
 
• The oil is high in **protein** and has a **nutty flavor**, making it a popular choice for **salad dressings and marinades**.
 
• Lentil oil is also used in **skincare products** for its** moisturizing and nourishing properties**.
 
• The oil is rich in **antioxidants and vitamins**, making it beneficial for overall health and well-being.
 
• Lentil oil is a good source of** essential fatty acids**, which are important for maintaining healthy skin and hair.
 
 
 
• **Rhodamine**
 
 
• **​​**Rhodamine is a **fluorescent dye** that is commonly used in **microscopy **and** cell imaging**.
 
• It is also used as a** tracer dye** in environmental studies to track the movement of **water and pollutants**.
 
• Rhodamine dyes are known for their** bright pink to red color**, making them useful in various applications such as **inkjet printing **and **textile dyeing**.
 
• The dye has been used in **medical research **to visualize and study biological processes within **cells and tissues**.
 
• Rhodamine dyes are also used in the manufacturing of **security inks and anti-counterfeiting** **measures** for documents and currency.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT antimicrobial drugs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Antacids.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs.

 
 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs. Instead, they are medications that neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve symptoms of indigestion, heartburn, or acid reflux.
 
• They do not directly target microorganisms but rather work on the acidity level in the stomach.
 
• Common antacids include substances like calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and aluminum hydroxide.
 
 
 
• **Antibiotics -** 
 
 
• Antibiotics are antimicrobial drugs that specifically target and kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria.
 
• They are used to treat bacterial infections and work by interfering with bacterial processes, such as cell wall synthesis or protein production.
 
• Examples include penicillin, tetracycline, and amoxicillin.
 
 
 
• **​****Antiseptics **- 
 
 
• ​Antiseptics are substances applied to living tissues, such as skin, to reduce the risk of infection.
 
• Unlike disinfectants, antiseptics are safe for use on living tissues and are used to clean wounds, cuts, and surgical sites.
 
• Examples include iodine, hydrogen peroxide, and rubbing alcohol.
 
 
 
• **Disinfectants** - 
 
 
• ​Disinfectants are chemical substances used to eliminate or reduce the number of microorganisms on surfaces and inanimate objects.
 
• They are not typically used on living tissues but are effective against bacteria, viruses, and fungi.
 
• Common disinfectants include bleach, hydrogen peroxide, and alcohol-based solutions.

questions.question: Biogas is an excellent fuel as it contains up to 75% ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**methane.**__

__
 
• The percentage of methane in biogas is **75 %.**
 
• Biogas consists mainly of methane (CH₄)** 75% **and carbon dioxide (CO₂)** 25%.**
 
• Biogas is produced by using organic material, which is broken down with the help of bacteria in an anaerobic environment in the absence of oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biogas** is processed in dome type structure. 
 
• The bio plant has a dome-like structure built with bricks. 
 
• A slurry of organic waste and water is made in the mixing tank.
 
• Then it goes to the digester.
 
• The digester is a sealed chamber in which there is no oxygen.
 
• **Anaerobic micro-organisms** that do not require oxygen decompose or break down complex compounds of the cow-dung slurry.
 
• After the biogas is released and leftover slurry can be used as manure.

questions.question: Various parts of plants, vegetation and organic waste are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Biomass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Various parts of plants, vegetation, and organic waste are called Biomass**__. 
 
• **Biomass** is organic, meaning it is made of** material that comes from living organisms, such as plants and animals.**
 __
 
• The most common biomass materials used for **energy are plants, wood, and waste.**
 
• These are called **biomass feedstocks.**
 
• Biomass energy can also be a non-renewable energy source.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fossil fuels **include coal, petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, bitumens, tar sands, and heavy oils.

 
 
• All contain carbon and were formed as a result of geologic processes acting on the remains of organic matter produced by photosynthesis, a process that began in the Archean Eon (4.0 billion to 2.5 billion years ago).
 
 
 
• **Nuclear energy** is the energy in the nucleus, or core, of an atom.
 
 
• A nuclear reactor, or power plant, is a series of machines that can control nuclear fission to produce electricity.
 
• The fuel that nuclear reactors use to produce nuclear fission is pellets of the element uranium.
 
 
 
• **Solar energy** is radiant light and heat from the Sun that is harnessed using a range of technologies such as solar power to generate electricity, solar thermal energy including solar water heating, and solar architecture.

questions.question: Who suggested that life evolved from simple inorganic (abiotic) molecules?

__
 
• JBS British scientist Haldane suggested in 1929 that life may have evolved from simple inorganic molecules that were present on Earth shortly after its formation.
 
 
• He hypothesized that conditions on Earth at the time, which were far from those of today, could have given rise to the more complex organic molecules needed for life.
 
• The first primitive organisms would arise from further chemical synthesis.​
